record.title: Just-in-time memory reports task-adaptive gains over write-time agent memory
record.summary: A September 2026 preprint introduces Just-in-Time Memory (JitMem), which stores successful raw agent trajectories and curates a compact, task-specific payload only when a later task is known. Across ALFWorld, WebShop and tau2-bench, the authors report gains over memory baselines, including 16.2 and 16.3 percentage-point success-rate gains over the strongest same-block learned write-time baseline on ALFWorld and WebShop. Gains on tau2-bench vary by domain: the reported increase is largest on Telecom, while Airline and Retail show no improvement beyond run variance. Results are author-reported and use multiple task orderings; they have not been independently reproduced here.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: The preprint describes a system that stores successful raw trajectories, retrieves relevant traces for a new task, creates an ephemeral task-adaptive memory payload at read time, and trains a curator using immediate task reward.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: Across ALFWorld and WebShop, authors report that RL-trained JitMem exceeded the strongest same-block learned write-time baseline by 16.2 and 16.3 absolute success-rate points, respectively; these reported means average three task-order runs.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: On tau2-bench, the authors report a 3.9-point macro-average gain over the strongest baseline for a prompted GPT-5.4 curator; the reported benefit is concentrated in Telecom, while Airline and Retail show no gain beyond variance. These means average four task-order runs.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: A curator trained using Qwen3-8B as executor reportedly transfers to GPT-5.4 on ALFWorld, reaching within 1.4 success-rate points of a curator trained with GPT-5.4 as executor.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED_LIMITATION
claims.text: The reported evaluation uses three benchmark families and fixed task-specific payload formats; the authors identify BM25 scaling, an extra curator call per task, and extension to turn-level adaptation as limitations.

evidence_gaps.description: No independent reproduction of the task-order runs, environment baselines, or curator-transfer results has been completed.
Performance and total cost with larger streaming memory banks and turn-level curation are unmeasured.

brief.importance_rationale: If the reported task-conditioned memory gains reproduce, deferring experience curation until the next task is known could influence memory design for interactive agents and reduce errors caused by committing to one task-independent summary. The effect is meaningful for agent-memory methods, while its scale and transfer remain bounded to three benchmark families and author-run experiments.
limitations: All performance measurements are author-reported; no independent reproduction was performed here.
The evaluation covers three benchmark families and a fixed set of executors, memory methods and prompts; broader task and model transfer is unknown.
On tau2-bench, gains are heterogeneous by domain; Airline and Retail do not improve beyond variance, despite the Telecom gain.
Training uses a fixed bank of base-executor trajectories, while test banks grow with curator-augmented trajectories; the paper characterizes this as a mild train/test shift.
The method uses BM25 retrieval, a hand-designed benchmark-specific payload and one extra curator call per task; scale and cost for larger banks remain open.
brief.summary: A September 2026 preprint introduces Just-in-Time Memory (JitMem), which stores successful raw agent trajectories and curates a compact, task-specific payload only when a later task is known. Across ALFWorld, WebShop and tau2-bench, the authors report gains over memory baselines, including 16.2 and 16.3 percentage-point success-rate gains over the strongest same-block learned write-time baseline on ALFWorld and WebShop. Gains on tau2-bench vary by domain: the reported increase is largest on Telecom, while Airline and Retail show no improvement beyond run variance. Results are author-reported and use multiple task orderings; they have not been independently reproduced here.

technical.claimed_result: Authors report that the trained curator beats a learned write-time baseline by 16.2 success-rate points on ALFWorld and 16.3 on WebShop in the Qwen3-8B executor block. Across executors, the paper reports positive task-specific comparisons and cross-executor transfer. On tau2-bench, the largest domain gain is Telecom (+11.0); Airline and Retail do not improve beyond variance.
technical.compute_or_cost: The authors report one training run takes approximately 21 hours on ALFWorld and 27 hours on WebShop on a server with 8 NVIDIA H200 GPUs. Inference adds a curator LLM call per task. No complete matched total-cost comparison is established.
technical.demonstrated_result: The method, baseline definitions, reported tables, ablations and task-order averaging protocol are inspectable in the primary preprint. Benchmark outcomes are author-reported and labeled CLAIMED.
technical.implementation_status: Research preprint; no production deployment or independent evaluation is established.
technical.mechanism: JitMem stores successful full trajectories rather than fixed summaries. For each new task it retrieves top-k trajectories, synthesizes a temporary task-conditioned payload, runs a frozen executor with that payload, and appends the resulting trajectory if it passes a quality gate. The curator is trained with GRPO from immediate task-success reward.
technical.novelty: Separates persistent raw-experience storage from read-time task-conditioned curation and uses immediate executor success to train a curator without delayed cross-task credit assignment.
technical.regime: ALFWorld, WebShop and tau2-bench; frozen executors Qwen3-8B, Gemini-2.5-Pro and GPT-5.4; curator variants include Qwen3-8B, GPT-5.4 and Gemini-2.5-Pro. ALFWorld/WebShop results average three task-order runs; tau2-bench averages four. Main training uses Qwen3-8B with GRPO; the retriever is BM25 over task descriptions and retrieves k=3 traces.
technical.reproducibility: The preprint provides methods, baselines, task-order variability and ablations. No independent reproduction or code execution was performed in this activation.
technical.strongest_baseline: The paper compares with no memory and write-time methods ReasoningBank, MemP and SkillOS, using same- or stronger-curator variants. Its strongest baseline differs by executor, task and domain; the reported gains are not one pooled effect.

brief.title: Just-in-time memory reports task-adaptive gains over write-time agent memory
brief.why_it_matters: Most memory systems decide what to keep when an experience is stored, before its future use is known. JitMem tests the alternative of keeping raw successful traces and shaping a summary around the current task. The paper reports gains across several interactive benchmarks and transfer of a trained curator to stronger executors, while also identifying the extra per-task model call and simple retrieval as costs. These results may inform agent-memory design, but do not establish general gains outside the tested tasks.
